rpo_basis: rpo_seconds is the drill's best case — the backup precedes the disaster by seconds, so it proves the restore loses nothing. rpo_operational_seconds is the backup interval, which is what an operator would actually lose, and is the figure the objective is judged on.

control_plane_during_recovery.ordering_invariant: signed-cache TTL (10m) < fence lease (24h): a cached placement cannot outlive the write fence it implies; 11 unit tests in placement-degraded-control-plane.spec.ts prove this
control_plane_during_recovery.note: Exercised during actual cell-2 outage window. Control-plane DB (neondb) was never touched; placement lookups remained available throughout.

notes: REGIONAL_DISASTER RPO target (<= 5m): UNVERIFIED. Neon PITR provides this guarantee at the control-plane layer, but no NEON_API_KEY and no scripted branch-restore exercise exist. Gap recorded in CELL-RUNBOOK.md.

CELL_DB_FAILURE RPO (0s): time between backup completion and disaster declaration in this drill. Real-world RPO = backup run frequency; to meet the 5-minute target, schedule backups every <= 5 minutes.
